facts.text: Incorporated on February 17, 1937, Rudy originated as a railroad stop and agricultural hub, named for early settler George Rudy who established the town's first post office in 1883.

A devastating tornado struck on September 27, 1927, destroying the school, homes, businesses, and Methodist church, though rebuilding efforts included a Works Progress Administration community building in the 1930s.
Before 1803, Osage hunters used the area, and after the 1817 Cherokee cession, the land opened to white settlers in 1828.
To request a permit, you'll need to contact the local building authority at Rudy’s City Hall, where the administrative staff can guide you through the application process.
